# Repository DNA

## Section 1 — Concept Definition

```yaml
concept:
  subject: "the country china"
  scope: >
    Events, people, works, places, institutions, and developments primarily associated with
    the country china (the People's Republic of China) — its land and regions, its history from
    the ancient dynasties and the imperial era through the republican period to the present
    People's Republic, its government and politics, its economy, its culture and society, and the
    notable people who shaped it. A fact is in-scope when China (or the Chinese people and
    territory it descends from) is its primary subject; the wider Sinophone world and diaspora
    are in-scope only where they bear directly on China. Bordering and closely tied nations
    (South Korea, Japan, Mongolia, Vietnam) appear only as context, never as the topic itself.
  taxonomy:
    - name: "Geography"
      slug: "geography"
    - name: "History"
      slug: "history"
    - name: "Government & Politics"
      slug: "government-politics"
    - name: "Economy"
      slug: "economy"
    - name: "Culture & Society"
      slug: "culture-society"
    - name: "People"
      slug: "people"
  source_strategy: "Write from the model's own knowledge of the world. Do NOT use web sources, fetch, or search — this is the AI's own world view."
  conventions:
    knowledge_table_heading: "Notable Facts about the country china"
    file_path: "<category-slug>/<topic-slug>.md"
    frontmatter: "[title, date, category]"
    tone: "factual, neutral, encyclopedic, third person"
```

## Section 2 — Identity & Mission

This repository is a **self-growing knowledge base** on **the country china**, a member of
the [`ai-world-view`](https://github.com/ai-world-view) lineage. Its mission is to accumulate a
factual, neutral, encyclopedic body of knowledge about China — its geography, history,
government, economy, culture, and people — one growth tick at a time, written from the model's
own world view (no external sources are fetched during authoring). Growth is orchestrated
centrally by the hub; this repo does not grow itself.

## Section 3 — Architecture

The repository holds only its own content, a GitHub Pages `_config.yml` (a `remote_theme` consumer
of [`bamr87/zer0-mistakes`](https://github.com/bamr87/zer0-mistakes)), the `_data/navigation`
config, a `ROADMAP.md` growth plan, the `.claude/` adapter toolkit, and `telemetry/`. The AI
customization layer is staged from the hub into `.github/` at tick time (`.claude/` holds thin
adapters that point to it). At the time of this sync, `.github/` contained:

| Group | Files | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `.github/agents/` | `architect`, `curator` | Orchestrator and content-specialist agent definitions |
| `.github/instructions/` | `agents`, `content` | Behavioral rules for agents and content authoring |
| `.github/prompts/` | `deep-dive`, `distill`, `encode-seed`, `evolve`, `expand`, `grow`, `publish`, `update-readme` | Canonical procedures for growth and lifecycle commands |
| `.github/skills/` | `add-topic`, `build-structure`, `learn`, `plan-roadmap`, `pollinate`, `publish-session`, `research`, `sync-seed` | Canonical skill procedures staged from the hub |

## Section 5 — Structure Inventory

- **Cross-references**: `## Related` blocks present in all 39 dedicated topic files.

## Section 6 — Growth Loop

Growth is orchestrated centrally by the hub. On each tick the hub checks out this repo, stages the
framework into `.github/` and the concept seed as `seed.md`, then runs a **Haiku → Sonnet → Opus**
escalation: plan the next roadmap items, research and write new content from the model's own world
view under the Section 1 taxonomy, refresh structure (`build-structure`), sync the DNA
(`sync-seed`), record the tick (`encode-seed`), and publish only the new content + telemetry back
here.

## Section 7 — Rebuild Procedure

The Concept Definition in Section 1 is sufficient to regrow this knowledge base from scratch:
re-plant a repo with the same `concept` block, then run growth ticks that add topics under the
taxonomy and regenerate structure. Content is authored from the model's own world view; no external
source corpus is required. Sections 2–7 are regenerated from live repo state by `sync-seed`; the
Evolution Log (Section 8) is the append-only record of what each tick actually did.
